_what: CONTAINER-SIDE WALL-CLOCK DEADLINES that this tree already carried when watchdog_ceiling_semantics_check gained its container-deadline class. A RATCHET BY MEMBERSHIP: it may only ever SHRINK. Nothing here is blessed and nothing here is exempt -- every entry is printed on every run with its remedy, and any site NOT in this file is refused with rc 1.
_why_it_exists: `_container_exec.run_in_container` puts a GNU `timeout -k 5 <deadline>` in front of the tool INSIDE the container. That removed the orphan (a host-side timeout kills the docker exec CLIENT and leaves the tool running) and introduced a worse thing: a raw wall-clock SIGTERM of a job that may be working perfectly -- the class vibe-ic#2051 removed everywhere the supervisor could reach.
_measured: vibe-ic#2083, 2026-09-07, 8HD-8, image sha256:8c5694ab (0.3.48). The magic LEF extraction of a 35 MB GDS, run with nothing in front of it, needs 5187.5 s at a steady 1.000 CPU-s/s and finishes cleanly (exit 0, DIGITAL_LEF_WRITE_DONE, a 21494-byte abstract with 84 pins). The 900 s deadline digital_hardmacro_gen carried lands at 17.4% of that job, and every LEF of that size was being cut in the middle and booked `magic did not complete`. Re-measured at main 353e9f512a09 after the NDA history rewrite: 4 sites, the fourth added by f39dd4e03. CONVERTED 2026-09-07 (lane cza3pin, 8HD-9, vibe-ic#2117): the A3 row is gone -- `analog_a3_netlist_emit.verify_with_ngspice` now enters the container through `run_in_container_supervised`, so 3 sites remain. THE REGISTER SHRANK WITH THE FIX, which is the only direction it moves.
_the_remedy_for_every_entry: Route the launch through `_container_exec.run_in_container_supervised`: identity stamp then `exec`, NO clock, `container_tree_probe` as the stillness signal, and `_docker_watchdog.kill_supervised_job` reaping BY IDENTITY on a stall -- so the orphan the deadline prevented is still prevented, and a computing tool is never cut. The deadline value becomes a RECORDED ceiling (announced once, the job runs on).
